text: A B+ tree keeps every row in its leaves and links the leaves left to right, so a range query descends once to the first key and then scans the linked leaves.
When a leaf overflows the node is split in two halves and the middle key is copied into the parent; a split can propagate up to the root, which grows the tree.
BM25 ranks documents by term frequency saturated with the parameter k1 and normalized by document length with the parameter b, times the inverse document frequency of each query term.
An inverted index maps every term to its posting list, the sorted identifiers of the documents that contain it, so a query only reads the lists of its terms.
HNSW builds a hierarchy of proximity graphs; a search starts at the top layer and greedily walks towards the query vector before descending to denser layers.
The R-tree groups nearby points into minimum bounding rectangles and prunes every rectangle that cannot contain an answer to a spatial query.
El informe mide el archivo secuencial contra el heap file y el hash extensible con inserciones, búsquedas y borrados por clave.
